Subject: Re: Unusual latency / 5xx spike on Hightower production

Avery —

We're seeing a sustained latency regression and a rise in 5xx errors across multiple endpoints that use the Redwood hosted model. Snapshot from our monitoring (last 2 hours):
- p50: ~120ms (ok)
- p95: 1.8s (expected ~600ms)
- 5xx rate: 2.2% (baseline <0.1%)
- Throughput: our request TPS is down ~15% compared to typical peak windows

This is impacting checkout NLU for a subset of customers. We briefly routed a small fraction to our fallback endpoint and saw normal latency, so it looks like something in the Redwood serving path is spiking. Can you confirm what you're seeing on your side and advise on immediate mitigation? Our SREs have collected traces and can share logs — attaching initial capture.

We need an agreed temp mitigation plan (throttles / fallback / rate limits) + an ETA for a fix. Please escalate to your ops and leadership as needed.

Thanks,
Rachel Park
Head of Platform Reliability
Hightower Retail

Team — quick triage notes from the war-room:

What we see (initial):
- Spike originated ~06:50 UTC (~2h ago) and sustained for ~90m.
- GPU queue depth increased on the host group serving Hightower model variant (routable pool id: rp-hightower-1).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped (prefix-sensitive workload from a new scheduled batch job at the customer side).
- CPU/memory on edge routers normal; network egress latency not elevated.
- 5xx types: majority are 503/504 (upstream overload/timeouts) + a small fraction of model-inference OOMs.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Increased autoscale headroom for rp-hightower-1 (provision +2 GPUs) — visible capacity coming up now.
- Applied conservative short-term connection throttles for large-batch clients from Hightower (internal rate limit rule id: RL-HT-03).
- Enabled kernel fallback to lower-latency quantized path for that variant (minor quality delta — documented).

Planned next steps (30–90m):
- Confirm whether customer batch job can be rate-smoothed — flagged to Rachel.
- Run targeted canary rollback to previous model build for 5% of traffic if errors persist.
- Collect and share trace file (attached: request_trace_20270320.json) and I/O histograms.

Impact: early indicators show p95 dropping toward expected range (now ~720ms at time of writing) and 5xx trending down. Still monitoring.

If we need to escalate to emergency dedicated capacity (longer-term), will coordinate with finance/ops.

— David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: War-room summary & exec status — Hightower incident (21 Mar 2027)

Folks — final summary from today's coordination. I'm sending this to leadership and the customer thread for transparency.

Timeline / status:
- Incident began: 2027-03-21 06:50 UTC (customer monitoring alert).
- Mitigations applied: +2 GPU headroom to rp-hightower-1, short-term client throttles (RL-HT-03), quantized kernel fallback enabled, targeted canary rollback prepared.
- Current metrics: p95 ~700–750ms; 5xx <0.5%; throughput recovering to baseline.

Customer impact: partial degradation on checkout NLU for a minority of sessions; Hightower followed our recommendation to route critical flows to fallback for ~20 minutes which helped stabilization.

Action items / owners:
- David: continue monitoring rp-hightower-1 and confirm full rollback only if canary is clean (ETA 45m).
- Neha: compile post-incident trace summary and runbook notes for Hightower SOC review (ETA EOD).
- Marissa / Grace: finalize customer-facing incident summary and run it by Rachel; coordinate follow-up account health call.
- Avery: escalate to Ops lead for discussion of reserved capacity options if these traffic patterns are recurring.

Decision log: we will not perform a full rollback immediately — prefer controlled canary + targeted capacity for safety. If error-rate resurges >1% persistently, we move to emergency dedicated capacity and open a billing/contract discussion.

Next customer update: 30–45 minutes or earlier if conditions change.

Thanks to the team for rapid coordination.

— Avery Johnson
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
